title: Cleopatra
passages: Cleopatra was born in 69 BC in Alexandria, a busy port city in Egypt with a famous lighthouse glowing over the sea. Her family was a Greek DYNASTY called the Ptolemies, and they had ruled Egypt for nearly 300 years. Alexandria held a great library full of scrolls, and SCHOLARS came from many lands to study stars, medicine and maths. Cleopatra was a keen learner. Ancient writers say she spoke up to nine languages, and she was probably the first in her family to learn Egyptian. At about 18, she became queen, sharing the throne with her younger brother.

Cleopatra is best known as the last active PHARAOH of ancient Egypt, a ruler who worked hard to keep her country free from mighty Rome. A turning point came in 48 BC. Her brother had pushed her off the throne, so stories say she was smuggled into the palace wrapped in a bundle of bedding to meet the Roman leader Julius Caesar. He helped her win back her crown. Later she formed an ALLIANCE with another Roman, Mark Antony. Their side lost a great sea battle at Actium in 31 BC. Cleopatra died in 30 BC, aged 39, and Egypt became part of the Roman Empire.
